note: The OLG adequately covers the $125 earned income change reporting threshold (Change Reporting – Overview: 'earned income that is more than $125.00 per month') and prospective budgeting BEACON procedures (Entering, Changing, and Ending Earned Income in BEACON: Prospective tab, Calculate, Refresh). Income averaging policy is addressed in Types of Earned Income > Income Averaging (mandatory vs. elective averaging, migrant exclusion). However, several FNS 1063 requirements lack OLG coverage: (1) Vacation/sick pay classification — FNS specifies counting it as income in the month received, as the same source unless terminated, or as a non-recurring lump sum if from a terminated source paid in one sum. The OLG has no guidance on vacation/sick pay treatment. (2) The OLG's lump sum content (Noncountable Income, SNAP Asset Guidelines) covers nonrecurring lump sums generally but does not address the specific rule linking final vacation/sick pay from terminated employment to lump sum treatment. (3) FNS requires using Section 722 procedures to determine whether new or terminated source income counts in the budget — the OLG has no equivalent policy guidance for when income from starting/ending jobs enters or exits the budget calculation. (4) The formal FNS definition of 'interim change' (recalculation from household-reported changes or agency-discovered changes including SSA/SSI COLAs and TANF mass adjustments, requiring documentation of both awareness and timely action) is not stated in the OLG, though the COLA mass change process is covered procedurally in a separate section (SSA COLA Overview). The OLG's change reporting and income sections are BEACON-procedure-heavy but lack the policy logic layer that FNS 1063 establishes for income source classification and budget timing.
